influences.name: William Faulkner
influences.context: I will return to the same books over and over again, even if it's not in the context of preparing for a new record or trying to find inspiration for a new record. I do still find myself on these ten-year cycles with books where I'm like, "Now it's time to reread The Sound and the Fury."

influences.name: Hayao Miyazaki
influences.context: You even said that one of the new songs "Rovenshere" (which is probably a pun on "rove and share," to come back to the importance of stories) had a lot of Miyazaki imagery, right? Yes! Right after I mentioned this to you, a few other people said the same thing – that the piano was reminiscent of the score in Spirited Away and evoked that kind of imagery

influences.name: Devendra Banhart
influences.context: I'm trying to think of a male musician I've ever been compared to. Like early, early days: Devendra Banhart. He and I had some aesthetic similarities: the music was pulling in some ways to a similar place.

influences.name: Lola Montez
influences.context: The title track was inspired by Lola Montez, an itinerant Irish-born burlesque dancer in the 19th century who became mistress to the king of Bavaria and used her power to advance a liberal agenda. Newsom became interested in Montez because she had lived for two years in Grass Valley, where Newsom was born; mostly, though, she found herself identifying with her as a woman and a performer.
